entries.title: My shape is not closed
entries.q: open contour; not closed; gap; wont extrude; cannot extrude; extrude error; sketch has open; broken outline; ends not touching
entries.fix: Find the gap. Drag one loose end onto the other end until it snaps.

steps.t: Zoom in on each corner with the scroll wheel. Small gaps can be hard to see.
Click Tools > Sketch Tools > Check Sketch for Feature. Click Check. Read the result.
Drag one loose end onto the other end. Check that the ends join.
Click an extra line you do not need. Press Delete.
Click Features > Extruded Boss/Base again.

entries.why: A solid extrude makes a 3D shape from a closed outline. A gap can stop this lesson’s extrude.

entries.title: It says my sketch has multiple contours or lines crossing
entries.q: multiple contours; self intersecting; lines crossing; overlapping lines; two outlines; contour error; intersect
entries.fix: Check which outlines you need. Remove only the extra lines. Keep any holes you meant to draw.

steps.t: Look for lines that cross or stick out past a corner.
Click Sketch > Trim Entities. Choose Power trim.
Drag across each extra piece with the left mouse button held down.
Check for lines drawn on top of each other. Ask a TA before removing a line you are unsure about.
Click Tools > Sketch Tools > Check Sketch for Feature. Click Check.

entries.why: An outline inside another can make a hole. Side-by-side outlines can make separate bodies. Crossing or extra lines may stop the tool.

entries.title: I left my sketch and cannot get back in
entries.q: exited sketch; get back into sketch; edit sketch; left sketch; cant edit sketch; sketch gone; change my sketch; go back to sketch
entries.fix: Click the sketch in the left tree. Click Edit Sketch.

steps.t: Find the tree: the step list on the left.
Click the arrow next to Boss-Extrude1 if you already made a 3D shape. Look for Sketch1 inside it.
Click Sketch1 in the tree.
Click Edit Sketch, the pencil icon.
Click Exit Sketch when you finish.

entries.why: Exit Sketch ends drawing mode. Edit Sketch lets you change the drawing later.

entries.title: I messed up so badly I want to delete everything and start over
entries.q: start over; delete everything; delete part; messed up; ruined; new part again; restart
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z once. Check what changed. You can also edit the step that went wrong.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z once. Check the result before pressing it again.
Right-click the wrong feature, a step in your part. Click Edit Feature.
Right-click the sketch if its lines need changes. Click Edit Sketch.
Ask a TA before deleting work you may still need.

entries.why: Undo or Edit Feature can keep the steps that already work.

entries.title: My numbers are huge or weird, like 25.4
entries.q: millimeters; mm; wrong units; numbers huge; 25.4; metric; inches; units; decimals
entries.fix: Click the units in the bottom-right corner. Choose IPS for inches.

steps.t: Find the unit label at the bottom-right. MMGS uses millimeters.
Click the unit label. Choose IPS, which uses inches.
Check the sizes shown. Changing units does not scale your shape.
Check each size against your assignment. Change only values that do not match.
Click Options, the gear icon. Click Document Properties > Units. Set Length decimals to .123.

entries.why: Every size in this project is in inches. A 2 you typed in millimeters is 2 mm, about the thickness of a coin. The unit system decides what your typed numbers mean.

entries.title: My sketch turned red or yellow, or says Over Defined
entries.q: red lines; yellow lines; over defined; overdefined; conflict; sketch red; cannot solve; sketchxpert
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z to undo the last size or drawing rule. Check whether the red marks clear.

steps.t: Look for Over Defined at the bottom. It means some drawing rules conflict.
Press Ctrl+Z once. Check whether the red lines clear.
Check the red or yellow size labels. Ask a TA which rule to remove.
Click Tools > Sketch Tools > SketchXpert. Click Diagnose. Review a proposed change before clicking Accept.

entries.why: Each dimension is a rule. If a line is 2 inches long AND its two ends are dimensioned 2.5 inches apart, both cannot be true. SolidWorks shows the conflict in red.

entries.title: What do blue and black lines mean?
entries.q: blue lines; black lines; under defined; fully defined; line colors; why blue
entries.fix: Blue lines can still move. Black lines have fixed sizes and positions. Either color can work.

steps.t: A blue line can still move. Check its size before dragging it.
Add needed sizes with Smart Dimension. Black lines have their size and position set.
Read Under Defined or Fully Defined at the bottom. These words describe how much can still move.

entries.why: Dimensions and relations are drawing rules. They hold sizes and positions in place.

entries.title: My part disappeared or I cannot find it
entries.q: cant see part; disappeared; lost; gone; zoomed out; blank screen; where is my part; nothing there
entries.fix: Move the mouse over the drawing area. Press F to fit the part in the view.

steps.t: Move the pointer over the part area. Press F to fit the view.
Press the spacebar if the view is still unclear. Double-click Isometric, a view from a corner.
Find the rollback bar in the left tree. Right-click it. Click Roll to End.
Open Solid Bodies in the tree. Right-click a hidden body. Click Show.

entries.why: Zoom, a hidden body, or the rollback bar can hide a part from view. Check the left tree if F does not help.

entries.title: There is a red X or a yellow triangle in the tree
entries.q: red x; error; yellow triangle; warning; rebuild error; feature failed; fillet failed; cut failed; failed; what wrong; exclamation
entries.fix: Point at the first warning in the left tree. Read its message. Right-click that step. Choose Edit Feature.

steps.t: Find the first marked feature from the top of the tree. Start there.
Hold the pointer over its mark. Read the message.
Right-click the feature. Choose Edit Feature for settings or Edit Sketch for lines.
A yellow triangle is a warning to check. A red X means the step failed.
Check the Fillet size if the error names a fillet. Try a smaller radius, the size of the round.

entries.why: Features are built in order, top to bottom. If an early one changes, a later one can lose the edge or face it was attached to, and it fails.

entries.title: Things in my tree are gray, or there is a yellow and black line in the middle
entries.q: grayed out; gray features; rollback bar; yellow black line; features missing; part went back
entries.fix: Right-click the yellow-and-black bar in the left tree. Choose Roll to End.

steps.t: Find the rollback bar in the left tree. It marks where the part stops building.
Right-click the bar. Click Roll to End.

entries.why: The rollback bar marks how far the model is built. Steps below it are paused.

entries.title: It keeps drawing lines every time I click
entries.q: keeps drawing; cant stop drawing; line tool; extra lines; stop tool
entries.fix: Press Esc to stop the drawing tool.

steps.t: Press Esc. Press it again if the drawing tool stays on.
Click an extra line you do not need. Press Delete.

entries.why: The Line tool stays on so you can draw a chain of lines. Esc or a double-click ends the chain.

entries.title: A tool opened that I did not choose
entries.q: tool opened by itself; random tool; enter key; repeat command; popped up
entries.fix: Press Esc to stop the tool. Enter can repeat the last tool.

steps.t: Press Esc to stop the tool.
Click the red X on the open settings panel if you want to cancel that tool.

entries.why: In SolidWorks the Enter key means do the last command again. That is handy once you know it and confusing until you do.

entries.title: I cannot click the face or edge I want
entries.q: cant select; wrong face; clicks wrong thing; select edge; select face; behind; hidden face
entries.fix: Press F6 if a selection filter is on. Otherwise, right-click near the item. Choose Select Other.

steps.t: Turn the view by dragging with the middle mouse button held down.
Right-click near the item. Choose Select Other. Click the item you want in the list.
Zoom in with the scroll wheel to separate nearby edges.

entries.why: A selection filter limits what you can click. Select Other helps when faces and edges overlap in the view.

entries.title: The buttons or tabs at the top disappeared
entries.q: toolbar gone; tabs missing; commandmanager; buttons gone; sketch tab missing; features tab missing; ribbon gone
entries.fix: Right-click near the top tabs. Check Enable CommandManager. Turn on the missing tab.

steps.t: Right-click a top tab, such as Features or Sketch.
Point to Tabs. Check the missing tab.
Right-click an empty spot at the top if all tabs are gone. Check CommandManager, the top tool panel.

entries.why: The tabs can be turned off with a right-click, so they are easy to lose by accident. Nothing is broken.

entries.title: The list on the left disappeared
entries.q: tree gone; left panel gone; featuremanager missing; list missing; side panel
entries.fix: Press F9 to show the list on the left.

steps.t: Press F9 to show the left tree.
Finish or cancel the open tool if settings cover the tree. Use the green check to finish or the red X to cancel.

entries.why: F9 hides or shows the left panel. A tool’s settings can also cover the tree until you finish the tool.

entries.title: My view is tilted and I cannot draw straight
entries.q: tilted; sideways; rotated; crooked; cant see sketch flat; view wrong; upside down
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+8 while editing the sketch. This looks straight at the sketch.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+8 while editing a sketch. This faces the sketch straight on.
Press the spacebar for other views. Double-click Front.

entries.why: Looking straight at the sketch makes its shapes easier to see. Turning the view does not tilt the sketch plane.

entries.title: My extrude went the wrong way, or only to one side
entries.q: wrong direction; one side; not centered; mid plane; flip; reverse; extrude backwards
entries.fix: Right-click the Extrude in the left tree. Choose Edit Feature. Change Direction 1 to Mid Plane.

steps.t: Right-click Boss-Extrude1 in the tree. Click Edit Feature.
Open the end-setting list under Direction 1. Choose Mid Plane.
Type the full thickness, such as 0.500 inches. Half extends each way.
Click the green check.

entries.why: Mid Plane grows the part equally both ways from the sketch, so the front and back of your hook match and it stays centered.

entries.title: My part has two bodies (Solid Bodies(2))
entries.q: two bodies; solid bodies 2; separate pieces; not connected; merge result; floating
entries.fix: Edit the last Extrude. Check Merge result. The new shape must touch the old shape to join it.

steps.t: Open Solid Bodies in the tree. A count of 2 means two separate 3D shapes.
Right-click the last Extrude. Click Edit Feature. Check Merge result.
Check whether the new shape touches the old shape. Edit its sketch if the two should touch.

entries.why: This lesson needs one solid body: one connected 3D shape. Two separate bodies may be correct in other projects.

entries.title: My circle dimension shows R instead of a diameter
entries.q: radius; diameter; R instead of; circle dimension; show diameter
entries.fix: Right-click the size label. Choose Display Options > Display as Diameter.

steps.t: Right-click the size label.
Point to Display Options. Click Display As Diameter, which shows full width.
Click a full circle when adding its size with Smart Dimension. Check for the diameter symbol.

entries.why: Radius is half the full width. Diameter is the full width. This lesson gives the circle’s diameter.

entries.title: SolidWorks froze or closed
entries.q: froze; crashed; not responding; closed; lost my work; recover
entries.fix: Wait briefly if SOLIDWORKS is busy. If it closed, reopen it. Look for Document Recovery.

steps.t: Wait 30 seconds. SOLIDWORKS may still be working.
Reopen SOLIDWORKS if it closed. Look for Document Recovery; a saved recovery copy may be available.
Open a recovery copy if one is listed. Use File > Save As to keep it.
Press Ctrl+S every few minutes as you work.

entries.why: Recovery copies may be available. They depend on the backup settings. Save often with Ctrl+S.

entries.title: When I typed a dimension, the whole shape jumped or flipped
entries.q: shape jumped; flipped; went crazy; distorted; dimension moved everything; exploded
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z. Move the shape close to the size you need. Add the size label again.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z once. Check the shape.
Place lines near the size you want before adding sizes.
Set the large sizes first. Set the small sizes next.

entries.why: When you type a number, SolidWorks moves whatever lines are free to move. If the sketch was far from that size, a lot has to move and it can flip.

entries.title: The box to type my dimension did not pop up
entries.q: no box; cant type number; dimension box; modify box; type value
entries.fix: Double-click the size label to edit its value.

steps.t: Double-click the size number.
Type the value. Press Enter.

entries.why: The automatic value box depends on a setting. A size label can usually be edited by double-clicking it.

entries.title: My sketch is on the wrong plane
entries.q: wrong plane; lying flat; top plane; sideways part; edit sketch plane
entries.fix: Exit the sketch. Right-click it in the left tree. Choose Edit Sketch Plane. Select Front Plane.

steps.t: Right-click the sketch in the tree.
Click Edit Sketch Plane.
Click Front Plane in the tree. Click the green check.

entries.why: Build the hook outline on the Front Plane so Front view shows its shape and Mid Plane grows it evenly.

entries.title: It says rebuild, or there is a traffic light icon
entries.q: rebuild; traffic light; needs rebuild; not updated
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+B to update the part.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+B to update the part.
Press Ctrl+Q if it still needs a full update.

entries.why: After a change, SolidWorks recalculates the part. Rebuild makes it catch up.

entries.title: I dragged an arrow and my part changed size
entries.q: dragged arrow; changed size by accident; blue arrow; instant3d
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z once. Check the size again.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z once. Check the size.
Double-click a size number to change it on purpose. Type the new value. Press Enter.

entries.why: Those arrows let you drag a feature bigger or smaller. Dragging by accident changes the real size.

entries.title: Start a new part
entries.q: new part; new file; start; begin; create part; open solidworks
entries.fix: Click File > New. Choose Part. Click OK. Set inches. Save with your last name.

steps.t: Click File > New.
Choose Part. Click OK.
Check for IPS at the bottom-right. Click the unit label to choose IPS if needed.
Press Ctrl+S. Put your last name in the file name. Click Save.

entries.why: Saving first means autosave and Ctrl+S protect your work from the first minute.

entries.title: Switch to inches
entries.q: inches; units; ips; change units; set units
entries.fix: Click the units in the bottom-right corner. Choose IPS.

steps.t: Click the unit label at the bottom-right.
Choose IPS, which uses inches.
Click Options, the gear icon. Click Document Properties > Units. Set Length decimals to .123.

entries.why: Every hook rule is in inches, to three decimals.

entries.title: Start a sketch
entries.q: start sketch; new sketch; draw; begin drawing; front plane; sketch plane
entries.fix: Click Front Plane in the left tree. Click Sketch.

steps.t: Click Front Plane in the left tree.
Click Sketch on the small bar or the top Sketch tab.
Press Ctrl+8 if the view does not face the sketch.
Find the origin, the red starting point. Start your first circle there.

entries.why: A sketch is a flat drawing. A plane is a flat guide. This lesson uses Front Plane.

entries.title: Draw lines, circles and arcs
entries.q: draw line; circle; arc; rectangle; draw shape; sketch tools; curve
entries.fix: Choose Line, Circle, or Arc on the Sketch tab. Click to draw. Press Esc to stop.

steps.t: Click Circle on the Sketch tab. Click the center. Move outward. Click to set the edge.
Click Line. Click a start point. Click each corner. Press Esc to stop.
Click Tangent Arc for a smooth curve from a line. Click the line end to start it.
Check that the ends join where you want a closed outline.

entries.why: Do not worry about exact sizes while drawing. Draw the shape roughly, then set exact sizes with Smart Dimension.

entries.title: Set an exact size (Smart Dimension)
entries.q: dimension; size; exact size; smart dimension; measure in sketch; set length; diameter; center to center
entries.fix: Click Smart Dimension on the Sketch tab. Click an item. Place the label. Type the size. Press Enter.

steps.t: Click Smart Dimension on the Sketch tab.
Click a line for its length or a circle for its full width. Click two circles for the space between their centers.
Move the pointer to place the size label. Click.
Type the value in inches. Press Enter.
Press Esc when you finish adding sizes.

entries.why: The sketch is only rough until you dimension it. Dimensions are how you control the real size, and how you change it later.

entries.title: Change a size after I extruded
entries.q: change size; change dimension; edit dimension; resize; make bigger; make smaller; modify
entries.fix: Double-click the part to show its sizes. Double-click a size label. Type the new value. Press Enter.

steps.t: Double-click the feature in the tree. Its size labels appear.
Double-click the number you want to change.
Type the new value. Press Enter.
Press Ctrl+B to update the shape.

entries.why: This is the whole point of CAD: one number changes and the part updates.

entries.title: Leave the sketch
entries.q: exit sketch; leave sketch; finish sketch; done sketching; close sketch
entries.fix: Click Exit Sketch on the Sketch tab.

steps.t: Find Exit Sketch on the Sketch tab.
Click Exit Sketch to finish drawing.

entries.why: You can go back in at any time with Edit Sketch.

entries.title: Make it 3D (Extruded Boss/Base)
entries.q: extrude; make 3d; thickness; boss; turn sketch into part; extruded boss base
entries.fix: Click Extruded Boss/Base on the Features tab. Choose Mid Plane. Type the depth. Click the green check.

steps.t: Click the Features tab.
Click Extruded Boss/Base to give the sketch thickness.
Click your sketch if asked to choose one.
Choose Mid Plane under Direction 1. Type the thickness your assignment asks for.
Click the green check.

entries.why: Extruded Boss/Base adds depth to a closed outline. Mid Plane adds equal depth on each side.

entries.title: Sketch on a face of my part
entries.q: sketch on face; draw on part; face sketch; add to face
entries.fix: Click a flat face on the part. Click Sketch.

steps.t: Click a flat face on the part.
Click Sketch on the small bar.
Press Ctrl+8 to face the sketch.
Draw a closed outline. Use Extruded Boss/Base to add material or Extruded Cut to remove it.

entries.why: Any flat face can be a sketch plane. That is how you add a raised rim, a pocket or a boss.

entries.title: Cut a hole or a pocket (Extruded Cut)
entries.q: cut; hole; pocket; remove material; extruded cut; subtract
entries.fix: Draw a closed shape on a flat face. Exit the sketch. Click Extruded Cut on the Features tab. Set the depth. Click the green check.

steps.t: Draw a closed outline in a sketch on the face.
Click Features > Extruded Cut.
Choose Through All for a hole through the part. For a pocket, choose Blind. Type its depth.
Check the preview. Click the direction arrow if the cut points away from the part.
Click the green check.

entries.why: A cut is an extrude that removes material instead of adding it.

entries.title: Round an edge (Fillet)
entries.q: fillet; round edge; round corner; smooth edge; radius edge
entries.fix: Click Fillet on the Features tab. Type a small radius. Select the edges. Click the green check.

steps.t: Click Features > Fillet to round an edge.
Type the radius, the size of the round. For example, try 0.060 inches.
Click the edges you want to round.
Click the green check. Try a smaller radius if it fails.

entries.why: A fillet rounds an edge. Radius sets how large that round is.

entries.title: Bevel an edge (Chamfer)
entries.q: chamfer; bevel; angled edge; 45 degree edge
entries.fix: Open the arrow next to Fillet. Click Chamfer. Type a distance. Select the edges. Click the green check.

steps.t: Open the arrow under Fillet on the Features tab. Click Chamfer to make a sloped edge.
Type a distance. Click the edges.
Click the green check.

entries.why: A chamfer is a flat bevel. Some downward-facing bevels need less print support; check the printer settings.

entries.title: Make both sides match (Mirror)
entries.q: mirror; symmetric; both sides; copy to other side; match
entries.fix: Click Mirror on the Features tab. Choose Front Plane. Pick the step to copy. Click the green check.

steps.t: Click Features > Mirror to copy across a plane.
Click the Mirror Face/Plane box. Click Front Plane in the tree.
Click the Features to Mirror box. Click the cut or boss to copy.
Click the green check. Use Mirror Entities for lines inside a sketch.

entries.why: A hook pulled in the middle should be the same on both faces, or it twists.

entries.title: Copy an outline inside itself (Offset Entities)
entries.q: offset; wall; rim; copy outline; inside outline; border
entries.fix: Click Offset Entities on the Sketch tab. Type the gap size. Select the edges. Check the direction. Click the green check.

steps.t: Start a sketch on the face.
Click Sketch > Offset Entities to copy edges nearby.
Type a distance. Click the edges to copy.
Check Reverse if the copy goes the wrong way. Click the green check.

entries.why: Offset Entities copies edges at a fixed gap. It helps make walls with an even width.

entries.title: Erase part of a line (Trim)
entries.q: trim; erase part of line; cut line; remove extra; power trim
entries.fix: Click Trim Entities on the Sketch tab. Choose Power trim. Drag across only the pieces you want to remove.

steps.t: Click Sketch > Trim Entities.
Choose Power trim.
Drag across unwanted pieces with the left mouse button held down.
Press Esc when finished.

entries.why: Overlapping circles and lines leave extra pieces inside your outline. Trim removes them so the outline is one loop.

entries.title: Draw a centerline
entries.q: centerline; center line; construction; dashed line; symmetry line
entries.fix: Open the arrow next to Line on the Sketch tab. Click Centerline.

steps.t: Open the arrow next to Line. Click Centerline, a guide for your drawing.
Click a start point. Click an end point. Press Esc.

entries.why: A centerline is a drawing guide. It does not become part of the solid shape.

entries.title: Make two things touch, line up, or be tangent
entries.q: tangent; smooth; coincident; line up; horizontal; vertical; equal; relation
entries.fix: Hold Ctrl while clicking two items. Choose a drawing rule in the left panel.

steps.t: Select two items while holding Ctrl.
Choose a rule under Add Relations on the left. Tangent means a smooth join. Coincident means touching. Equal means the same size. Horizontal means level.
Press Esc when finished.

entries.why: Relations are rules between drawing items. Tangent joins a curve smoothly, without a sharp corner.

entries.title: Measure my part
entries.q: measure; how big; check size; distance; diameter; thickness; center distance
entries.fix: Click Measure on the Evaluate tab. Click the items you want to check.

steps.t: Click Evaluate > Measure.
Select two circle edges to check their center distance.
Select one circle edge to check its full width.
Select two faces to check the distance between them.
Click empty space to clear the selection. Close Measure when finished.

entries.why: Measure checks the real part, which is what the inspection will check.

entries.title: Turn, zoom and move the view
entries.q: rotate; turn; spin; zoom; pan; move view; look around; view
entries.fix: Hold the middle mouse button to turn the view. Scroll to zoom. Hold Ctrl and the middle button to slide the view.

steps.t: Drag with the middle mouse button held down to turn the view.
Roll the scroll wheel to zoom.
Drag while holding Ctrl and the middle mouse button to slide the view.
Press F to fit the part. Press the spacebar to choose a view.

entries.why: Moving the view never changes the part.

entries.title: Undo a mistake
entries.q: undo; go back; oops; mistake; ctrl z; redo
entries.fix: Press Ctrl+Z to undo one change. Press Ctrl+Y to redo it.

steps.t: Press Ctrl+Z once. Check what changed.
Press Ctrl+Y if you need to redo the change.

entries.why: Undo can reverse a recent change. Check the result; not every view or editing action can be undone.

entries.title: Change an extrude, cut or fillet
entries.q: edit feature; change extrude; change depth; change thickness; thicker; thinner; change fillet; edit cut
entries.fix: Right-click a step in the left tree. Click Edit Feature.

steps.t: Right-click the feature, a step in your part.
Click Edit Feature.
Change a setting. Click the green check.

entries.why: Every feature keeps its settings. You can change them any time.

entries.title: Find what is wrong with my sketch
entries.q: check sketch; what is wrong; find gap; find error; sketch problem
entries.fix: Click Tools > Sketch Tools > Check Sketch for Feature. Choose the tool you plan to use. Click Check.

steps.t: Open the Tools menu while editing the sketch.
Click Sketch Tools > Check Sketch for Feature.
Click Check. Read the result.

entries.why: It finds gaps, crossing lines and doubled lines faster than your eyes can.

entries.title: Save my part with the right name
entries.q: save; save as; name file; filename; lastname; where to save
entries.fix: Click File > Save As. Type a name with your last name. Choose your class folder. Click Save.

steps.t: Click File > Save As.
Type the name your assignment asks for, such as V1_SMITH.
Choose Part (*.sldprt) in Save as type.
Choose your class folder. Click Save.
Press Ctrl+S to save later changes.

entries.why: Save a SOLIDWORKS part as .SLDPRT. Keep it in your class folder so you can edit it later.

entries.title: Hide or show the planes
entries.q: planes; hide planes; show planes; squares in the way; plane clutter
entries.fix: Click View > Hide/Show > Planes.

steps.t: Click View > Hide/Show > Planes to show or hide the flat drawing guides.

entries.why: Planes are guides. Hiding them clears the view and does not delete them.
